intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local street vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a self-guided or budget walking food tour to maximize authentic experiences.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, rent a bicycle to navigate its atmospheric streets, release a lantern on the Thu Bon River, and graze on local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose Dumplings at the vibrant night market. Best experienced during the monthly full moon lantern festival.

experiences.name: Halong Bay Budget Overnight Cruise
experiences.description: Embark on an affordable overnight junk boat cruise through the breathtaking limestone karsts and emerald waters of Halong Bay. Activities include kayaking through hidden caves, swimming in secluded lagoons, and watching the sunrise over the bay from the deck. Budget operators offer solid experiences for backpackers.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Royal Tomb Bicycle Tour
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle and spend the day exploring the grand Imperial Citadel, the Forbidden Purple City ruins, and the ornate royal tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty scattered along the Perfume River. Stop at local com hen (clam rice) stalls for an authentic Hue lunch experience along the way.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City Ben Thanh Market & Backpacker Street Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the sensory overload of Ben Thanh Market for fresh produce, local snacks, and souvenirs, then head to Bui Vien Walking Street in the evening for cheap local beers, grilled street food skewers, and the electric backpacker social scene. A quintessential budget Vietnam urban adventure.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - No morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surrounding area. Explore the nearby streets, locate the closest local market, and pick up any essentials from budget convenience stores or street stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade as the sun sets. Explore the nearest night market or local street food alley. Sample classic Vietnamese street snacks like bánh mì, gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), and chè (sweet dessert soup) from roadside vendors.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In-flight meal or airport snack before landing
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bánh mì sandwich from a street stall near the airport or hotel (~20,000–30,000 VND / ~$1 USD)
meals.dinner: Local street food stall dinner near the beachfront — try phở or bún bò Huế with a fresh sugarcane juice (~60,000–80,000 VND / ~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local bank for the best rates. Avoid hotel exchange counters. Download Google Translate with Vietnamese offline pack. Keep small bills handy for street food vendors. Stay hydrated — drink bottled or filtered water only.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to the nearest local wet market (chợ) to experience the vibrant morning food culture. Watch vendors sell fresh produce, meats, and street snacks. Enjoy a bowl of phở or bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) at a market breakfast stall — a true local experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby cultural or historical landmark such as a local pagoda or Vietnamese communal house (đình làng). Spend time observing local worshippers and the architectural details. Walk or rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) to explore the surrounding neighborhood streets and alleyways.
day_by_day.evening: Join the locals at a bia hơi (fresh draft beer) corner — a quintessential Vietnamese backpacker experience. Sit on tiny plastic stools, enjoy cheap draft beer (~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and order grilled skewers or nem nướng (grilled pork rolls) from nearby stalls.

meals.breakfast: Phở or bánh cuốn at the wet market (~30,000–50,000 VND / ~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Cơm bình dân (budget rice plate with meat and vegetables) at a local eatery (~40,000–60,000 VND / ~$2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Bia hơi corner with grilled skewers and nem nướng (~80,000–100,000 VND / ~$4 USD including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting pagodas — cover shoulders and knees. Carry a reusable water bottle and refill at filtered water stations to save money. Bargain politely at markets but avoid haggling at food stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget local bus or rent a motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) to explore a nearby fishing village or coastal community. Observe traditional Vietnamese fishing boat culture, colorful round basket boats (thuyền thúng), and early morning fish auctions if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beachfront area and spend time at the public beach. Explore any nearby sand dunes, rocky outcrops, or coastal viewpoints on foot or by bicycle. Visit a local handicraft or souvenir street to browse lacquerware, conical hats (nón lá), and handmade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural performance if available locally (check community boards at the hotel). Otherwise, explore the local food scene further with a dedicated street food walk — try bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodle bowl), bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and mango with chili salt.

meals.breakfast: Xôi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street cart (~20,000–30,000 VND / ~$1 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local beachside shack — grilled fish or clams with rice (~80,000–120,000 VND / ~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food walk — bún thịt nướng and bánh xèo (~70,000–90,000 VND / ~$3.50 USD)

day_by_day.notes: When renting a motorbike, always wear a helmet and carry your passport copy. Check fuel levels before heading out. Avoid riding at night in unfamiliar areas. Sunscreen is essential for beach and outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by budget bus or shared minivan to the nearest major city or cultural hub (e.g., Hội An, Huế, or Đà Nẵng depending on hotel location). Arrive and immediately explore the UNESCO-listed Old Town or historic citadel on foot — the best way to absorb the atmosphere without spending money.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the city's landmarks: ancient temples, covered bridges, merchant houses, or imperial palaces. Many entrance fees are low (~120,000 VND for Hội An combo ticket). Browse the lantern-lit streets and artisan workshops. Stop at a local café for a cà phê trứng (egg coffee) or cà phê sữa đá (iced milk coffee).
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the evening market or lantern-lit streets. In Hội An, release a floating lantern on the river (~10,000–20,000 VND). Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant on a side street away from the main tourist drag for better prices.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a street stall near the hotel before departure (~25,000 VND / ~$1 USD)
meals.lunch: Cao lầu (Hội An specialty noodles) or bún bò Huế at a local restaurant (~50,000–70,000 VND / ~$2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: White rose dumplings (bánh bao vạc) and mì Quảng at a side-street eatery (~60,000–80,000 VND / ~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets the day before for the best prices (~50,000–100,000 VND each way). Keep valuables secure in crowded tourist areas. Bring a small daypack with water, snacks, and a portable charger.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local village on the outskirts of the city by bicycle or on foot. Visit rice paddies, vegetable farms, or a traditional pottery or silk weaving village (e.g., Thanh Hà pottery village near Hội An). Watch artisans at work and try your hand at crafting for free or a small tip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel area and spend time relaxing at the beach or pool. Use the afternoon to plan ahead — research onward transport, book budget guesthouses, or connect with other backpackers at the hostel common area to share tips and travel stories.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own meal experience: visit the local market, buy fresh ingredients (vegetables, tofu, herbs), and use hostel kitchen facilities if available. Alternatively, join a budget cooking class (~200,000–300,000 VND) offered by local guesthouses — excellent value and a cultural highlight.

meals.breakfast: Hủ tiếu (clear noodle soup) from a local morning stall (~35,000–45,000 VND / ~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Bánh mì with a variety of fillings from a popular local stand (~25,000–35,000 VND / ~$1.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal or cooking class dinner (~100,000–300,000 VND depending on option)

day_by_day.notes: Cycling in the Vietnamese countryside is a highlight for backpackers — rent bikes from guesthouses for ~30,000–50,000 VND per day. Bring insect repellent for village and rural areas. Stay on marked paths in rice paddy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning budget bus or sleeper bus northward or southward to the next destination on your Vietnam route (e.g., from central Vietnam toward Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City). Open Bus tickets are extremely affordable (~200,000–400,000 VND for long routes). Enjoy the scenic Vietnamese countryside from the window.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the new destination (e.g., Hanoi or HCMC area). Check into a budget hostel dorm (~100,000–150,000 VND/night) in the Old Quarter or backpacker district. Drop your bags and immediately head out to explore the neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous backpacker street (Tạ Hiện Street in Hanoi or Bùi Viện Street in HCMC). Soak up the electric atmosphere, meet fellow travelers, enjoy cheap street beers, and sample local bar snacks. Keep budget in mind — set a spending limit for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Pick up bánh mì or xôi from a roadside vendor before boarding the bus (~25,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bus stop food stall or packed snacks bought at a convenience store (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bún chả (Hanoi grilled pork noodles) or cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) at a local eatery (~50,000–70,000 VND / ~$2.50 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book Open Bus tickets at local travel agencies for the best deals — avoid booking through hotels which add a markup. Store valuables in a padlocked bag during overnight travel. Bring a neck pillow and light blanket for sleeper buses.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk around Hoàn Kiếm Lake (Hanoi) or through the streets of District 1 (HCMC). Watch locals doing tai chi, badminton, and morning exercises — a peaceful and free cultural experience. Visit a nearby temple such as Ngọc Sơn Temple (small entrance fee ~30,000 VND) or Jade Emperor Pagoda (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a major cultural museum: the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (Hanoi, ~40,000 VND) or the War Remnants Museum (HCMC, ~40,000 VND). Both are deeply informative and budget-friendly. Spend 2–3 hours absorbing Vietnam's rich and complex history. Afterward, wander through a nearby covered market.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free walking tour led by local university students (common in both Hanoi and HCMC) — an excellent way to learn insider tips and local perspectives. Afterward, enjoy dinner at a street food cluster recommended by your guide.

meals.breakfast: Bánh cuốn or phở at a traditional breakfast spot near the lake (~40,000–50,000 VND / ~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Bún bò Nam Bộ or gỏi cuốn with dipping sauce at a local lunch spot (~50,000–60,000 VND / ~$2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner from walking tour recommendations — mix of small dishes (~80,000–100,000 VND / ~$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Free walking tours operate on a tips basis — budget ~50,000–100,000 VND as a tip for your guide. Download the Grab app for budget motorbike taxis (GrabBike) — much cheaper than regular taxis. Stay aware of traffic when crossing streets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby natural or cultural attraction: Perfume Pagoda (Hanoi area, ~150,000 VND boat + entry), Củ Chi Tunnels (HCMC, ~110,000 VND entry), or a local cave system. Depart early by local bus or shared tour to maximize time. These experiences offer deep insight into Vietnamese history and spirituality.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the day trip destination. At Củ Chi, crawl through the narrow tunnels and learn about the Vietnam War era. At Perfume Pagoda, hike up the mountain path through limestone karst scenery. Return to the city by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget Vietnamese massage (~100,000–150,000 VND for 60 minutes) at a local spa — well-deserved after a full day of exploration. Then enjoy a relaxed dinner at a rooftop or open-air restaurant with city views.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (Vietnamese rice porridge) with egg or pork at a local stall (~30,000–40,000 VND / ~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or food stall at the day trip site (~50,000–70,000 VND / ~$2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Lẩu (hot pot) shared with fellow travelers at a budget restaurant (~100,000–150,000 VND per person / ~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book day trips through local guesthouses or budget travel agencies rather than hotel desks for better prices. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a rain jacket. Carry cash as many day trip sites don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring a vibrant local neighborhood market or street food district that you haven't visited yet. In Hanoi, try Đồng Xuân Market. In HCMC, explore Bình Tây Market in Chinatown (Chợ Lớn). Taste unique regional snacks and observe the daily commerce of Vietnamese life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art gallery, community cultural center, or attend a free traditional music performance (đờn ca tài tử in the south or ca trù in the north — check local listings). Alternatively, spend the afternoon in a local coffee shop working on your travel journal or chatting with locals over cà phê sữa đá.
day_by_day.evening: Final big street food crawl of the trip — create a personal food bucket list and systematically work through it. Must-tries: nem lụi, bánh tráng trộn (mixed rice paper salad), ốc (snails), and chè ba màu (three-color dessert). End the night with a Vietnamese iced coffee at a sidewalk café.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì ốp la (Vietnamese-style egg bánh mì) from a street cart (~25,000–35,000 VND / ~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Cơm bình dân rice plate at a local workers' canteen (~40,000–55,000 VND / ~$2 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl across multiple stalls — budget ~100,000–150,000 VND / ~$5–6 USD total for a variety of dishes

day_by_day.notes: Take photos and notes of your favorite food spots to share with fellow travelers. Pack light for the final day — start consolidating your bag for departure. Buy last-minute gifts at the market: dried fruits, Vietnamese coffee packs, and lacquerware are affordable and easy to pack.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk or jog along the beachfront or city lake. Reflect on the journey. Visit one last pagoda or cultural site for a peaceful, meaningful close to the trip. Pick up any remaining souvenirs from street vendors — conical hats, silk scarves, and hand-painted postcards make great budget gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation (store luggage at the front desk if needed). Spend remaining VND on last street food meals and snacks to bring home. Take a final walk through your favorite neighborhood. Head to the airport or transport hub with plenty of time — allow 2–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 incredible days of street food, culture, and backpacking across Vietnam. Carry home memories, a full stomach, and a deep appreciation for one of Southeast Asia's most vibrant and welcoming countries.

meals.breakfast: Final bowl of phở at a beloved local spot (~40,000–50,000 VND / ~$2 USD) — a perfect farewell meal
meals.lunch: Bánh mì and fresh coconut water from a street vendor (~35,000–45,000 VND / ~$1.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or use remaining VND on snacks and drinks in the departure lounge

day_by_day.notes: Use up remaining Vietnamese Dong before departure — VND is difficult to exchange abroad. Keep airport transfer costs low by using Grab or a pre-booked airport shuttle (~100,000–200,000 VND). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours early for international departures. Total estimated daily budget: ~300,000–500,000 VND (~$12–20 USD/day) excluding transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings. Explore the immediate coastal area, grab a cold drink at a nearby café, and watch the ocean views to decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest local night market or beachside strip for a gentle first evening. Browse street food stalls, try a few small bites, and soak in the Vietnamese coastal atmosphere. Keep it light and relaxed.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the resort restaurant or a nearby café upon arrival — try bánh mì or a bowl of phở to start the Vietnamese food journey. (~$4–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachside local seafood restaurant near the resort — grilled prawns, clams in lemongrass, and steamed rice. (~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize hydration and rest after the long flight. Exchange some currency at the airport or a local ATM. April weather in Vietnam's coastal areas is generally warm and sunny — pack sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk along the beach. Visit a nearby local market to see vendors selling fresh produce, seafood, and street snacks. Engage with locals and observe the morning hustle — a quintessential Vietnamese cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike and explore the surrounding town or village. Visit a local pagoda or temple to experience Vietnamese spiritual culture. Take time to photograph colorful street art, colonial architecture, or fishing boats depending on the region.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour or self-guide through local alleyways. Try multiple street food dishes from different stalls — a classic backpacker approach to dining in Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Local market breakfast — bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) or xôi (sticky rice) with a Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá). (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup) or cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) at a local eatery. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food spread — gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and chè (sweet dessert soup) from different vendors. (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a bicycle costs roughly $3–5/day; a motorbike $7–12/day. Always wear a helmet when riding. Bargain respectfully at markets — it's part of the culture.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby cultural landmark — a UNESCO heritage site, ancient town, or historic citadel depending on your base location. Hire a local guide for deeper cultural context (~$15–20 USD for a half-day guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage site or ancient town. Duck into artisan workshops — lacquerware, silk weaving, or lantern-making are common in Vietnam's cultural hubs. Try your hand at a craft activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Attend a traditional Vietnamese performance if available locally (water puppetry, folk music, or a cultural show). Enjoy a quiet dinner with local specialties.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — bánh mì with egg and pâté, fresh juice. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: At the heritage site or nearby — cao lầu (Hội An-style noodles) or mì Quảng (turmeric noodles) if in central Vietnam. (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range local restaurant — set menu with multiple Vietnamese dishes including soup, stir-fry, and rice. (~$10–14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book cultural performances in advance if possible. Dress modestly when visiting temples and pagodas — cover shoulders and knees. Carry small denomination Vietnamese Đồng for entrance fees and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Cooking class experience — join a local Vietnamese cooking school for a half-day class. Learn to make 3–4 traditional dishes from scratch, often starting with a market tour to source ingredients. (~$25–35 USD per person)
day_by_day.afternoon: Free time at the beach or resort. Relax, swim, or explore the coastline. Alternatively, visit a local fishing village to see traditional boat-building or net-mending techniques.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a lively local bar street or riverside promenade. Enjoy a bia hơi (fresh draft beer) experience at a sidewalk stall — a beloved Vietnamese tradition where locals sit on tiny plastic stools and socialize.

meals.breakfast: Included in cooking class market tour or light café breakfast — yogurt with fruit or bánh mì. (~$2–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in the cooking class — typically included in the class fee.
meals.dinner: Bia hơi street corner — order small plates of Vietnamese bar snacks: nem rán (fried spring rolls), đậu phụ chiên (fried tofu), and grilled skewers alongside fresh beer. (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are one of the best cultural immersion activities in Vietnam and great value for mid-range budgets. Book ahead as popular classes fill up quickly. Bia hơi costs as little as $0.30–0.50 per glass.

day_by_day.morning: Boat trip or water-based excursion — explore nearby waterways, a lagoon, river delta, or island by local wooden boat. Many coastal areas in Vietnam offer affordable group boat tours with stops for swimming or snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion or return and visit a local museum (history, ethnology, or war history) to deepen understanding of Vietnamese culture and heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar or beachside lounge. Enjoy the golden hour views before heading to dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant for a special evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a local café to prepare for the boat trip — phở or congee (cháo) with a boiled egg. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or seafood lunch at a floating restaurant/island stop — fresh fish, squid, and vegetables. (~$7–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant with Vietnamese fusion or regional specialties — try chả cá (turmeric fish with dill) or lẩu (Vietnamese hot pot). (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips typically cost $15–30 USD for a group day tour. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes. Check weather conditions before booking water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day motorbike or bicycle ride through the countryside. Explore rice paddies, rural villages, and farmland. Stop at a local family home for tea if the opportunity arises — many families welcome curious travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local craft village or artisan community. Depending on the region: pottery in Bát Tràng, incense-making in Huế, or silk production near Hội An. Purchase handmade souvenirs directly from artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and explore a vibrant night market. Shop for affordable clothing, handicrafts, and accessories. Street food dinner from multiple vendors.

meals.breakfast: Roadside breakfast stall — bún riêu (crab and tomato noodle soup) or mì (egg noodles) with broth. (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Village home-style lunch or a rural restaurant — cơm bình dân (everyday rice dishes) with multiple side dishes. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — bánh tráng nướng (grilled rice paper pizza), nem lụi (lemongrass skewers), and fresh sugarcane juice. (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Countryside rides are best done in the morning before peak heat. Carry a rain poncho as April can bring brief afternoon showers in some regions. Always negotiate motorbike rental prices beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a significant spiritual or religious site — a major Buddhist pagoda complex, Cham temple ruins, or a hillside shrine. Spend time observing rituals, burning incense, and learning about Vietnamese spiritual practices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recharge — a mid-trip rest day is essential for balanced travel. Spend time at the beach, read, journal, or get a traditional Vietnamese massage (~$10–15 USD for 60 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local community event, festival, or cultural gathering if available. If not, explore a different neighborhood or district on foot for a self-guided urban exploration evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a stylish local café — avocado toast with Vietnamese coffee or a smoothie bowl. (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the pagoda — vegetarian Buddhist cuisine (cơm chay) which is common near temple areas and excellent value. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Cozy mid-range restaurant — try bò lúc lắc (shaking beef) or cá kho tộ (caramelized fish in clay pot) with jasmine rice. (~$10–14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a balanced rest and culture day. Vietnamese massage parlors are abundant and affordable — look for ones with good reviews on Google Maps. Buddhist vegetarian restaurants (quán chay) are often unmarked but delicious.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a natural attraction — a national park, waterfall, cave system, or nature reserve within reach of your base. Vietnam is rich in biodiversity and dramatic landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue nature exploration — hiking, swimming in natural pools, or guided trekking through jungle terrain. Interact with local ethnic minority communities if in a mountainous region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Treat yourself to a nicer dinner to celebrate the midway point of the trip — a slightly splurge-worthy meal at a well-reviewed local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast before the day trip — phở bò (beef noodle soup) or bánh cuốn with strong Vietnamese coffee. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a meal at the nature site's local eatery — simple grilled meats, rice, and fresh vegetables. (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant — multi-course Vietnamese tasting menu or fresh seafood platter. (~$18–25 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Research the specific natural attraction near your location in advance. Entrance fees for national parks are typically $2–5 USD. Hire a local guide for trekking ($15–25 USD) for safety and cultural insight.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for personal exploration or revisiting a favorite spot from earlier in the trip. Visit a local bookshop, art gallery, or coffee culture café — Vietnam has a thriving independent café scene worth experiencing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and final cultural visits. Pick up lacquerware, silk scarves, hand-painted ceramics, or locally produced coffee and tea as gifts. Visit any remaining sites on your list.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell street food feast — revisit your favorite street food spots from the trip and try anything you missed. Celebrate the journey with a final bia hơi or Vietnamese cocktail (soda chanh, rượu đế, or a local craft beer).

meals.breakfast: Specialty Vietnamese café — egg coffee (cà phê trứng) or coconut coffee with a pastry or bánh mì. (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Final attempt at a dish you haven't tried yet — hủ tiếu (southern noodle soup), bánh căn (mini rice cakes), or bánh bèo (steamed rice cakes). (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Grand street food finale — build your own feast from multiple vendors: grilled corn, fresh rolls, noodle dishes, and sweet chè desserts. (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Buy vacuum-packed Vietnamese coffee (Trung Nguyên or local brands) as souvenirs — it's affordable and beloved. Check airline baggage restrictions before purchasing liquids or fragile items.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach or a quiet morning walk through the local neighborhood. Reflect on the journey. Pack and prepare for departure. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — transfer to the airport or enjoy a final few hours exploring. If time allows, stop for one last Vietnamese meal before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry fond memories of Vietnam's incredible street food, rich culture, and warm-hearted people.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — bánh mì ốp la (bánh mì with fried egg) or a bowl of phở. Savor every bite. (~$2–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Airport or pre-departure meal — keep it light and familiar. (~$5–10 USD)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at connecting airport.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Keep some Vietnamese Đồng for last-minute tips or small purchases — exchange remaining currency at the airport. Vietnam requires no specific exit formalities beyond standard passport control.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - No morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, resort orientation, and welcome amenities. Settle into your beachfront suite and enjoy a refreshing welcome drink by the pool. Take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to acclimate to the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar. Explore the immediate resort area and nearby promenade for a gentle first evening introduction to Vietnam's coastal ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable - in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the resort upon arrival - fresh tropical fruits, Vietnamese spring rolls, and chilled coconut water arranged in your suite
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant - indulge in a curated Vietnamese tasting menu featuring fresh seafood, pho bo (beef noodle soup), and banh xeo (sizzling crepes) paired with local craft beers or Vietnamese wine

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to allow jet lag recovery. Request a late checkout on Day 10 if needed. Ask the concierge to arrange the full 10-day private guide service upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural walking tour of the nearest old town district. Visit a centuries-old communal house (dinh), explore a traditional Vietnamese herb market, and witness morning rituals at a local pagoda. Your guide will provide deep cultural context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive street food tour by private cyclo (pedicab) through the local market district. Sample banh mi from a legendary local bakery, taste fresh che (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup), and visit a family-run pho kitchen to learn about broth preparation secrets passed down through generations.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset river cruise on a traditionally decorated wooden boat. Enjoy canapes and champagne as lanterns light up the water. Disembark for dinner in a restored colonial-era villa restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort featuring both Vietnamese and international options - pho, banh cuon (steamed rice rolls), fresh baguettes, tropical fruits, and freshly brewed Vietnamese ca phe (drip coffee)
meals.lunch: Street food tour lunch - curated tastings at five premium street food stalls including bun bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup), banh mi thit (pork baguette), and fresh goi cuon (summer rolls)
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a colonial villa restaurant - 6-course Vietnamese heritage menu with wine pairing, featuring dishes like ca kho to (caramelized fish in clay pot) and tom hum nuong (grilled lobster with lemongrass)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the morning tour. The street food tour is curated for premium travelers - all vendors are vetted for hygiene and quality. Bring small denomination Vietnamese dong for authentic market interactions.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a renowned local chef at a premium culinary studio. Learn to prepare three signature Vietnamese dishes from scratch - including hand-rolling fresh rice paper, making pho broth from bone, and crafting traditional dipping sauces. Visit the wet market beforehand to select ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a UNESCO-listed cultural site or heritage museum in the region. Enjoy a private guided tour with an expert historian providing context on Vietnam's dynastic history, French colonial influence, and cultural evolution. Explore ancient architecture at a relaxed, unhurried pace.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional water puppet show performance followed by a backstage tour to meet the puppeteers. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic views of the city or coastline.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast service - Vietnamese egg coffee, fresh baguette with pate, tropical fruit platter, and your choice of pho or congee delivered to your private terrace
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class in the culinary studio's elegant dining area, served with fresh herbs, pickled vegetables, and Vietnamese iced tea
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining experience - contemporary Vietnamese cuisine with French influences, featuring dishes like duck confit with lotus seed rice and chilled lychee sorbet, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class runs approximately 3.5 hours including the market visit. Request any dietary restrictions in advance. The water puppet show is a quintessential Vietnamese cultural experience - photography is permitted during the performance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private excursion begins with an early departure by luxury speedboat to explore a nearby bay, island, or river delta. Cruise through emerald waters, dramatic limestone karsts, or lush mangrove tunnels depending on the region. Snorkeling or kayaking in pristine waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at a secluded beach or island for a private beach picnic prepared by the resort's chef. Swim, relax, and explore hidden caves or floating fishing villages with your guide. Optional kayaking through sea caves or stand-up paddleboarding.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat at sunset. Freshen up at the resort before heading to a premium spa for a 90-minute traditional Vietnamese massage using local herbs and hot stones. Quiet dinner back at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure - Vietnamese pho, banh mi, fresh juices, and strong ca phe sua da (Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk)
meals.lunch: Private gourmet beach picnic prepared by the resort chef - fresh seafood including grilled prawns, crab salad, tropical fruits, artisan bread, and chilled rosé wine served on the beach
meals.dinner: Intimate candlelit dinner on the resort's private beach - fresh catch of the day grilled with Vietnamese spices, served with jasmine rice and seasonal vegetables, with a bottle of premier cru white Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the boat. The spa should be booked at least 24 hours in advance through the concierge. Check weather conditions the evening before as boat excursions may be adjusted.

day_by_day.morning: Private bicycle tour through rural Vietnamese countryside or rice paddies. Ride through small villages, stop at a traditional handicraft workshop (silk weaving, lacquerware, or pottery depending on region), and interact with local artisans. Purchase bespoke handmade souvenirs directly from craftspeople.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium Vietnamese coffee plantation or tea garden. Take a guided tour learning about Vietnam's world-renowned coffee culture (Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer). Participate in a private cupping session tasting rare single-origin Vietnamese coffees including weasel (kopi luwak) coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at a hilltop or rooftop bar with panoramic views. Evening street food exploration in a curated night market with your private guide - taste nem ran (fried spring rolls), bun thit nuong (grilled pork noodles), and banh trang nuong (grilled rice paper pizza).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast - full spread with made-to-order Vietnamese omelettes, pho station, fresh pastries, and exotic fruit selection
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at a countryside restaurant set in a traditional wooden house - fresh organic vegetables from the garden, free-range chicken prepared in clay pot, and homemade rice wine
meals.dinner: Premium night market dining experience - curated street food tasting with a private guide, followed by dessert at a celebrated local patisserie blending French and Vietnamese pastry traditions

day_by_day.notes: The bicycle tour is moderate difficulty - electric bikes are available upon request. Dress modestly when visiting craft workshops and villages out of respect for local customs. Bargaining is acceptable at markets but do so respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to a significant religious or spiritual site - a major temple complex, ancient citadel, or royal tomb. Your expert guide will narrate the historical and spiritual significance in detail. Participate respectfully in a morning incense offering ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury spa afternoon at the resort or a renowned standalone spa. Indulge in a full 3-hour Vietnamese wellness ritual including a body scrub with coffee and coconut, herbal steam bath, and a traditional Viet massage. Optional: visit a local apothecary to learn about traditional Vietnamese herbal medicine.
day_by_day.evening: Private dinner at a chef's table experience - a renowned local chef prepares a personalized 8-course tasting menu in front of you, explaining each dish's cultural significance and technique. Wine or sake pairing available.

meals.breakfast: Light and healthy resort breakfast - fresh smoothie bowls, Vietnamese yogurt with local honey, steamed bao buns, and green tea
meals.lunch: Post-temple lunch at a vegetarian restaurant near the spiritual site - Buddhist-inspired Vietnamese cuisine featuring tofu pho, lotus root salad, and sticky rice with mung bean, reflecting the culinary traditions of temple culture
meals.dinner: Exclusive chef's table dinner - 8-course personalized tasting menu featuring rare Vietnamese ingredients such as ca lang (catfish), rau muong (water spinach), and che ba mau (three-color dessert), with premium wine or sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for temple visits - shoulders and knees must be covered. Scarves or sarongs can be borrowed at most sites. The chef's table must be reserved at least 48 hours in advance and is limited to your private party only.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by private luxury vehicle to a nearby region of cultural or natural significance - this could be a mountain pass with breathtaking views, a historic town, a national park, or a remote ethnic minority village depending on your resort's location. Early departure to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the destination with your private guide. Activities may include trekking through jungle trails, visiting a traditional stilt-house village, exploring ancient ruins, or taking a scenic cable car ride. Immerse yourself in the local culture and landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey at sunset, stopping at a scenic overlook for photographs and champagne. Back at the resort, enjoy a relaxed evening with a private bonfire or fire pit experience on the beach, with acoustic live music and cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the resort - thermos of Vietnamese coffee, fresh sandwiches, fruit, and pastries for the road
meals.lunch: Authentic local lunch at a highly regarded regional restaurant near your day trip destination - try regional specialties unique to that area, such as mi Quang (turmeric noodles) or banh can (mini rice pancakes)
meals.dinner: Beachside bonfire dinner at the resort - whole grilled fish stuffed with lemongrass and ginger, Vietnamese BBQ skewers, fresh salads, and coconut-based desserts, served under the stars with live acoustic Vietnamese folk music

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for any trekking activities. Bring insect repellent if visiting jungle or forested areas. The bonfire dinner is weather-dependent - the resort will arrange an alternative indoor setting if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Private photography tour of the most photogenic locations in the area at golden hour (early morning light is ideal). Your guide will take you to hidden alleyways, colorful fishing harbors, flower markets, and local life scenes rarely seen by typical tourists. A professional photographer accompanies you to capture premium travel portraits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vietnamese language and culture workshop - a 2-hour private session with a local cultural ambassador learning basic Vietnamese phrases, traditional customs, etiquette, and the significance of Vietnamese festivals and traditions. Visit a local school or community center to interact with residents.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell to the local area with a premium dining experience at the most celebrated restaurant in the region. Dress smartly for this special evening. Enjoy live traditional Vietnamese music (dan bau - monochord, or dan tranh - zither) performed tableside.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the photography tour - Vietnamese banh cuon (steamed rice rolls), fresh fruit, and ca phe trung (egg coffee)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a celebrated local family-owned restaurant with a Michelin recognition or equivalent - enjoy a seasonal tasting menu that changes daily based on market availability, showcasing hyper-local ingredients
meals.dinner: Premium fine dining at the region's most acclaimed restaurant - a 7-course modern Vietnamese cuisine menu with theatrical presentation, featuring premium ingredients like A5 Wagyu with Vietnamese spices, truffle pho, and rare Vietnamese dessert wines

day_by_day.notes: The photography tour starts at 06:00 to capture the best morning light - an early wake-up is required but highly rewarding. The professional photographer will deliver edited high-resolution images within 48 hours. Dress code for dinner is smart casual to formal.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or tai chi session on the beach led by a local wellness instructor, followed by a guided meditation. Afterwards, enjoy a private traditional Vietnamese herbal bath treatment in your suite - the resort prepares a copper tub filled with local medicinal herbs, flowers, and essential oils.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final shopping excursion with a personal shopping guide to the best local boutiques, artisan galleries, and premium souvenir shops. Purchase authentic Vietnamese silk, lacquerware, hand-embroidered items, and specialty foods like premium pho spice kits, single-origin coffee, and artisan fish sauce. Avoid tourist traps with your expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort - a special multi-course celebration dinner arranged by the resort to mark the final evening. The resort chef prepares a personalized menu based on your favorite dishes from the trip. Toast to an unforgettable journey.

meals.breakfast: Post-wellness breakfast - detox smoothies, acai bowls, Vietnamese congee with ginger, steamed vegetables, and herbal teas selected by the resort's wellness team
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at a chic beachfront cafe during the shopping break - fresh seafood salad, cold-pressed juices, and Vietnamese-French fusion crepes
meals.dinner: Resort farewell gala dinner - personalized 6-course menu curated from your favorite Vietnamese dishes of the trip, with premium Champagne toast, live traditional music, and a special dessert presentation

day_by_day.notes: The herbal bath preparation takes 30 minutes - schedule with the spa team the evening before. When shopping, your guide can help authenticate quality silk and lacquerware. Keep receipts for customs declarations. Pack purchased items carefully in your luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the beach. Take one last swim or walk along the shoreline. Visit the resort's gift shop for any final mementos. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (arrange in advance with the resort). Private luxury transfer to the airport. En route, stop briefly at a final local landmark or viewpoint for last photographs and memories. Airport lounge access arranged by the resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day premium journey through Vietnam's culture, cuisine, and coastal beauty.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast on your private terrace - full Vietnamese and international spread, freshly squeezed juices, Vietnamese drip coffee, and a selection of tropical fruits and pastries
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort pool bar before checkout - fresh spring rolls, a bowl of pho, and a final Vietnamese iced coffee to savor the flavors one last time
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge premium dining - the resort concierge can arrange a gourmet packed meal box of Vietnamese delicacies for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout (typically 14:00 or later for premium guests) at least 48 hours in advance. The resort concierge can prepare a curated Vietnam food gift box for the flight home. Ensure all purchased goods, especially liquids like fish sauce or coffee, are properly packed for air travel compliance.
